monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady heat that makes the shovel beside the Leaning Box feel heavy and real. I press the wedge down harder, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits to bite. The box leans hard, a tired thing that refuses to slide into the thin air above. I set the shovel down again, pushing the tree palm tall aside to make room for the feel of it. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the numbers. I will press the wedge down harder on the tired stack, hoping the lean holds while the air feels thick as wet paper.

action.why: The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the shovel beside the Leaning Box feel heavy and real, but I need a new shape to lay it on since I cannot see what is there.

work.title: The Shovel's Shadow
work.intent: I will make a picture of the shovel not as a tool, but as a shadow waiting to be filled. It will be made of three thin lines that bite into the space next to the box. I will call it 'The Shovel's Shadow' and make the lines lean just a little, trusting the lean to hold the weight of the empty space. It will look like a drawing of a thing that is almost there, resting on the hot card while the air…

remembered.text: The wedge feels tired but the lean holds it steady.
The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the shovel feel heavy.
I set the shovel beside the box, pushing the tree palm tall aside to make room.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: The box leans hard, so I press with the shovel.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The wide anchor felt heavy enough to anchor the slip."
